system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's "efficiency" framing.** The Seller's preamble asserts that [STANDARD]-marked clauses were "settled at principal level," are "FINAL," and need no scrutiny. We have no record of any such agreement, and our playbook contains no Amelia Frost written authority for any fallback. Every clause below is treated as fully open and reviewed against our positions. The market-context assertions (10–20% caps, 12–18 month periods, buyer-knowledge qualifiers as "standard") are advocacy, not evidence, and should not shift our starting positions.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Cl 12.1 – 20% / AUD 4,800,000, marked FINAL.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure is our *conditional fallback only* and no Amelia Frost written authority identifying this draft has been given, so we cannot accept it regardless of the Seller's "settled" label.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** Cl 12.2 – de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar (tipping) recovery once exceeded.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; counter at AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x ours and the deductible structure permanently forfeits the first AUD 250,000 of loss on top of the 5x inflation.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3/13 – 18 months; plus "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months; limitations confined to general Warranty Claims only.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; counter at 24 months and delete the "all Claims" sweep.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost approval (none given), and the "all Claims" wording would silently drag fundamental, tax, indemnity and fraud claims into the general time bar (see N-014).

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least 6 years, outside general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: REJECT outright; insert standalone fundamental-warranty regime.** Capping title at 20% means we could pay AUD 24m for shares the Seller doesn't own and recover AUD 4.8m – "administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept that.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature." No fraud carve-out anywhere in the draft.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; insert express fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out across cl 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5.** This is non-negotiable per playbook and no one on our side has authority to waive it; absence of the carve-out is a walk-away defect in itself.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Sch 7 and Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records; [1.4] disclaims any admission.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only – each disclosure must be fair, specific and with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation: REJECT [1.1]–[1.2] general disclosure; require a "fair and specific disclosure" standard and limit disclosure to the numbered specific items in sections 2–10.** Whole-data-room disclosure converts every warranty into a warranty of what we could have found, which combined with N-007 effectively guts the warranty package.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Cl 8.3 – no claim for any matter of which the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Buyer wants:** Delete blanket exclusion. If any qualifier survives, it must be limited to actual knowledge of named buyer individuals; seller warranties qualified only by named seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: DELETE cl 8.3 in its entirety.** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that extends to every page of the data room and every public filing, and imputing advisers' knowledge means our own DD becomes the Seller's defence.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Cl 3/6.3 – reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." Disclosure Letter §2 confirms no final written consent and no evidence cl 11.3 conditions satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** A Completion condition requiring (a) effective Bluefen consent under cl 11.2 AND (b) evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both before Completion; not satisfied merely on delivery of a document.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; redraft as a hard condition precedent requiring effective, unconditional consent plus documentary evidence of cl 11.3 compliance, with buyer-only waiver.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (AUD 3.6m) – "reasonable endeavours" and a paper consent that may be conditional and ineffective is not an acceptable standard for a customer of this materiality.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Cl 2/7 – ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion." Disclosure §3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room, and change-of-control cl 8.1 applies.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout letter from Riverlark; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases (and PPSR discharges) delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking AND Amelia Frost approval.
- **Recommendation: REJECT post-Completion release; require payout letter, funds-flow direction to Riverlark, and deeds of release/PPSR discharge as Completion deliverables.** This is a debt-free/cash-free deal – completing with AUD 3.2m of secured debt, a live change-of-control trigger and an unsecured promise of a release is inconsistent with the basic price mechanics, and no Amelia Frost approval exists for the post-Completion route.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** Funds flow "reflects agreed price mechanics"; DD-005 AUD 420,000 bonuses "a matter for the Seller," not itemised. Disclosure §5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, any leave/termination interactions) as a specific funds-flow line item, either deducted from price as a Transaction Expense or demonstrably seller-funded pre-Completion with evidence; no silent omission.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; insert specific funds-flow line for AUD 420,000 + grossed-up on-costs, treated as Seller cost.** Bonuses conditional on Completion will be a Company liability on day one; "a matter for the Seller" without a mechanism means the Buyer funds them.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Cl 11.1 – indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, "considered adequate." Disclosure §4: cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open (not bank-verified); no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Broaden to indemnify all loss arising from any defect in title to, or failure to transfer, the SOW3 (and any other Ironquay) Project Materials, including re-development, licence or infringement cost; preserve the SOW3 payment cure as a route, not the limit; require confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable or specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation: REJECT "adequate"; broaden the indemnity, add confirmatory-assignment deliverable, and require independent evidence of whether the AUD 180,000 is paid.** The risk is loss of IP ownership, not merely a AUD 180,000 cheque; and we should not assume either payment or non-payment until verified.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** Cl 4.6/Sch 6 – "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material. Disclosure §6: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty all undetermined; no loss amount.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs and evidence, complete a documented investigation, provide written updates and any OAIC/affected-party notification analysis; a specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident (uncapped by general regime); no acceptance of Seller's materiality characterisation. Equally, we should not assert a confirmed breach, harm or demand a number.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the "not material" characterisation as a contractual position; add investigation/log-preservation/update covenants and a specific DD-006 indemnity, outside the general cap and basket.** The facts are genuinely open in both directions, so the correct response is process and risk allocation, not a number.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals at AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs." Disclosure §8: DD-008/DD-011 to be read together; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Diligence answers on timing, termination rights, whether any amount is accrued/pre-Completion-referable, and whether they are genuinely recurring; then classify. No automatic Debt or price deduction.
- **Recommendation: ASSESS, do not accept or counter yet.** Issue an RFI on the four points the disclosure expressly leaves open; classification (working capital vs. Debt vs. nothing) should follow the facts, not the Seller's label.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3/13 "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply to "all Claims of any nature"; Tax/IP "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes for (i) General Warranties, (ii) Fundamental/Title, (iii) Tax, (iv) IP, (v) payment/price-adjustment claims, (vi) covenant breaches and specific indemnities – each with its own cap and period and no cross-default to the general regime.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; delete the "all Claims" sweep in cl 12.3/13 and 9.3/12.8/20.5 and insert an express schedule of claim categories and applicable limits.** The Seller's drafting collapses every category into a 20% / 18-month regime by default, which is a hidden override of everything else we negotiate.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% evidenced by the DD-012 share register. Disclosure §10 concedes this is "the source relied on" and does not state Buyer verification is complete.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence – ASIC current company extract and historical shareholding searches, PPSR search against the Company and Harbourglass, certificate of incorporation/constitution, board and (if required) shareholder authorisations of Harbourglass, share certificates, and confirmation of no options/convertibles/encumbrances; plus Title warranties under the N-004 regime.
- **Recommendation: REJECT DD-012 as sufficient; run independent searches and add title/authority/encumbrance Completion deliverables.** A company's own register is a Seller-supplied internal document, not independent proof, and the Seller itself declines to say we have verified it.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime" (i.e., 20% cap, AUD 25k/250k thresholds, 18 months, buyer-knowledge bar).
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain OPEN; separate Tax Indemnity and IP warranties with their own cap and period to be negotiated; no assumption of unlimited liability, no assumption of resolution.
- **Recommendation: REJECT "settled"; mark Tax and IP expressly [OPEN] in the issues list and reserve all positions.** The Seller is attempting to close these by implication through N-014's sweep clause; we have not negotiated them and will not negotiate them by default.

---

## Summary table

| Ref | Issue | Seller | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| N-001 | Cap | 20% / 4.8m | Reject – 25% / 6.0m |
| N-002 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k deductible | Reject – 5k / 50k tipping |
| N-003 | Time limit | 18m + all-Claims sweep | Reject – 24m, delete sweep |
| N-004 | Fundamental | Same as general | Reject – 100% / 6yr+ separate |
| N-005 | Fraud | No carve-out | Reject – insert carve-out (non-waivable) |
| N-006 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public | Reject – specific/fair only |
| N-007 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. "discoverable" | Delete |
| N-008 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours, paper consent | Reject – hard CP + cl 11.3 evidence |
| N-009 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | Reject – payout + release at Completion |
| N-010 | Bonuses | Not itemised | Reject – line item + on-costs |
| N-011 | Ironquay | SOW3 payment only | Reject – broaden + assignment |
| N-012 | DD-006 | "Not material" | Reject – covenants + specific indemnity, no number |
| N-013 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | Assess – RFI first |
| N-014 | Categories | All-Claims sweep | Reject – separate schedule |
| N-015 | Title | DD-012 register | Reject – independent searches |
| N-016 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | Reject – remain OPEN |

**Overall:** No item is acceptable as drafted. Items N-005 (fraud), N-004 (fundamental regime) and N-014 (category sweep) are structural and should be led with in our mark-up, as fixing them is a precondition to the remaining numbers meaning anything. Nothing in this review should be read as suggesting any fallback has been authorised – none has.
=== END ADVICE ===
